title: H3412 (125th General Assembly): Firearms

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2022-12-08; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess125_2023-2024/prever/3412_20221208.htm (LegiScan doc 2617319))
provenance.note: Introduced text of 2022-12-08; no passage vote. In Section 4, 'ship, transport, or receive' is added to 16-23-500(A), the old fine/5-year penalty is struck for graduated terms, and subsection (D) is reworded (court with jurisdiction over offence punishable by more than one year); (D) and (E) not quoted.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Section 16-23-50(A)(2)): For a second offense, the offender is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, must be fined not more than two thousand dollars or imprisoned not more than three years, or both. For a third or subsequent offense, the offender is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction, must be fined not less than one thousand dollars and not more than two thousand dollars and imprisoned not more than five years.
Section 2 (new Section 16-23-540): Notwithstanding another provision of law, a person who steals a firearm is guilty of theft of a firearm and, upon conviction, is guilty of a felony and must be imprisoned not more than ten years.
Section 3 (new Section 16-23-545): (A) It is unlawful for a person convicted of a felony to possess a firearm in this State.
Section 4 (Section 16-23-500(B)): A person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction: (1) for a first offense, must be imprisoned not more than ten years; (2) for a second offense, must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum of five years, but not more than thirty years; and (3) for a third or subsequent offense, must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum of fifteen years, but not more than thirty years.
Section 5 (new Section 16-23-550): (A) It is unlawful for a person to possess a stolen firearm during the commission of a violent crime as defined by Section 16-1-60. (B) A person who violates this section is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction, must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum of ten years.
